    Scale and norm ideals of a bilinear form #

    The scale ideal is generated by all values of a bilinear form, and the norm ideal by its self-pairings. For a symmetric form, polarization gives twice the scale ideal inside the norm ideal. Spanning sets and bases provide generators for both ideals. Extending scalars extends both ideals; when 2 is a unit, the ideals coincide.

    The ideals are LinearMap.BilinForm.scaleIdeal and LinearMap.BilinForm.normIdeal, so B.scaleIdeal and B.normIdeal elaborate for B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M. The predicate LinearMap.BilinForm.IsScaleEven expresses parity relative to the scale ideal.

    References #

    • O. T. O'Meara, Introduction to Quadratic Forms, §82E.
    • Sungmun Cho, Group schemes and local densities of quadratic lattices in residue characteristic 2, Definition 2.1(b), for parity relative to a modular lattice's own scale.

        def LinearMap.BilinForm.IsScaleEven {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] (B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M) (π : R) :
        Prop

        A form is scale-even relative to π if its norm ideal lies in π times its own scale ideal. This is defined for arbitrary π. For symmetric dyadic modular forms at π = 2, it is the usual type II condition. The zero form satisfies the condition, giving the even convention for an empty Jordan constituent.
